Chapter 8: Courage in Action—Making a Difference, Big or Small.
You know, courage isn’t always that bold, roaring thing we see in movies. Sometimes, it’s the quiet choice to speak up, to try something new—or just to stand by what you believe, even when it’d be so much easier to keep your head down.
Think about those moments when things feel uncertain. That’s when courage gently nudges us from fear into action.
Let me tell you about a woman in the middle of her career—she’d been at her job for years, and honestly, she was feeling stuck. She noticed things at work that didn’t sit right with her: unfair policies, good people getting overlooked. At first, she convinced herself it wasn’t her place to say anything. But over time, that discomfort just wouldn’t go away.
Then, one day, she decided to do something about it. She called a meeting to talk about changes. Her voice trembled as she spoke, but something amazing happened—others chimed in. Together, they came up with new ideas. And you know what? Some of those ideas actually got put into practice.
She discovered something powerful: courage isn’t the absence of fear. It’s acting, even when you’re scared.
A lot of people think you have to make a huge splash to make a difference. But, most of the time, it’s the little, steady actions that really count. This woman, for example, started mentoring a new coworker, passing along what she’d learned. On weekends, she helped out at a local shelter. Each act was like a ripple, quietly spreading outward.
Here’s the thing: every single one of us can make a difference, no matter how small our actions might seem. Courage is contagious—when one person steps forward, others find the strength to do the same.
It’s easy to fall into the trap of waiting for the “right” moment or hoping that someone else will take charge. But honestly, there’s never a perfect time. The world starts to change when everyday people decide to act—even if their hands are shaking.
